name: trend_strength_adaptive_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: ADX (Average Directional Index) measures trend strength on a 0-100 scale but is typically used with static thresholds (>25 = trending). Instead of binary classification, this strategy uses ADX as a continuous scaling parameter for both indicator lookback and position size. When ADX is high (strong trend), use shorter EMA lookbacks (faster signals, ride the trend) and larger positions. When ADX is low (ranging), use longer lookbacks (fewer whipsaws) and smaller positions. The relationship is: EMA_lookback = max(5, 25 - floor(ADX/5)). This creates a continuously adaptive system rather than a discrete regime switch. The inefficiency persists because most implementations use ADX as a filter, not as a parameter modifier.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; stock ADX(14) must have been > 20 at least once in last 5 sessions (has trending tendency)

conditions: Adaptive_EMA > Adaptive_EMA_Slow (adaptive fast EMA above adaptive slow EMA)
long.confirmation: ADX_14 is rising: ADX_14 > ADX_14[3 bars ago]

short.confirmation: ADX_14 is rising: ADX_14 > ADX_14[3 bars ago]

exit.target: max(30, ADX_14 * 1.5) bps from entry — higher ADX = wider target
exit.stop_loss: max(20, ADX_14 * 0.8) bps from entry — higher ADX = wider stop
exit.trailing_stop: After target*0.6 profit, trail at target*0.4 from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: max(30, 90 - ADX_14) bars — higher ADX = shorter time stop (trends resolve faster)
exit.signal_exit: +DI/-DI cross against position OR ADX drops below 12 (trend exhausted)

risk.position_sizing: ₹(75000 + ADX_14 * 1000), capped at ₹1.5L — higher ADX = larger position

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (ADX warm-up needs ~28 bars) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: ADX must be > 15 (minimum trend strength to trade)
other_filters: Adaptive_EMA_Lookback must have been stable (not changed by >2) in last 5 bars to avoid signal instability

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — continuous ADX-parameter scaling is novel; most competitors use binary ADX thresholds; the adaptive system adds complexity that deters replication

weaknesses: Adaptive EMA lookback changes every bar as ADX fluctuates, causing EMA value discontinuities — when lookback jumps from 10 to 15, the EMA value can gap, creating false crossover signals
ADX-proportional position sizing increases exposure during strong trends, which is precisely when trend reversals are most damaging — the strategy takes its largest loss on the biggest reversal
The formula ADX_14 * 1.5 for target bps assumes linear relationship between trend strength and expected move magnitude, which is empirically not verified on 1-min NSE data
prior_art: Wilder's ADX (1978); Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA) uses similar efficiency ratio concept; ADX as a parameter modifier discussed in Ehlers 'Cybernetic Analysis for Stocks and Futures'
notes: Consider smoothing the Adaptive_EMA_Lookback by applying an EMA to the lookback value itself: Smoothed_Lookback = EMA(Adaptive_EMA_Lookback, 5). This prevents discontinuous jumps in EMA values when ADX fluctuates.
